passage: Suraj, why do I ask before I say no to your phone? Let me tell you about my daughter Sunaina. I'm Vikas, your uncle. She was eleven, chatting with an assistant on the family tablet, and I got worried and asked to see. Her face went stiff. "You don't trust me," she said, and I felt awful, because that wasn't it. I told her I was nervous, not angry. She turned the tablet toward me. She used it for spelling games and questions about frogs. We sat on the sofa and made three rules together: no giving out our address, tell me if anything feels strange, and no chatting at bedtime. Funny thing, after that she started showing me things without being asked.

qa.q: What did Sunaina use the assistant for?
qa.a: She used it for spelling games and questions about frogs.

qa.q: Why did Sunaina say, "You don't trust me"?
qa.a: She felt watched and hurt when her father asked to see her chats, and her stiff face showed it.

qa.q: What made the sharing work for Sunaina and Vikas?
qa.a: She showed him openly, he explained he was nervous rather than angry, and together they made three rules.

qa.q: What was it like for Vikas when Sunaina said he did not trust her?
qa.a: He felt awful, because asking came from his nervousness and not from anger.

grounding: A parent's worry leads a child to feel watched, then to share openly and agree rules together.

passage:
Counsellor's note, Thursday
Zainab's mother asked for a meeting because Zainab has been chatting with an AI chatbot every evening. Zainab sat with her arms folded. "She reads everything anyway," she muttered.
Her mother said, "I'm not spying. I just don't know what that thing says to you."
I asked Zainab if she would show us. After a pause, she did. Mostly quiz practice with her friend Jagdish, questions about black holes, and one long chat about feeling left out at lunch. Her mother went quiet at that one and touched her hand.
Together they agreed: the chatbot stays in the living room, no full name or school, and Zainab shows her mother anything that feels odd. By the end, Zainab's arms were unfolded.

qa.q: Where did they agree the chatbot would stay?
What did Zainab's folded arms suggest she was feeling?
qa.a: She felt watched and a little resentful about having her chats checked.

qa.q: What helped ease the worry for both of them?
qa.a: Zainab showed and explained what she uses the chatbot for, and they agreed on rules together.

qa.q: How does Zainab's mother see the chatbot?
qa.a: She is worried because she does not know what it says to her daughter; she is not trying to spy.

grounding: A counsellor's note shows a girl who feels watched when her worried parent asks to see her AI chats, and how sharing openly and agreeing rules builds trust.

passage:
Saturday night
Amma saw me on the AI app at ten o'clock and her face went all worried. "Show me what you're talking to it about." I felt like a spy had caught me. My ears went hot. I almost said "nothing" and switched it off.
But I showed her. Mostly it's me asking for story ideas and how to spell "necessary". And one where I asked why Payal and I fought. Amma read that one slowly and hugged me.
We made rules together: no AI after nine, never my full name or school, and I can bring the friend stuff to her too. She said she worries because it's new and she doesn't understand it yet.
Felt watched at first. Now I feel kind of trusted? 🙂
Gopika

qa.q: Which word did Gopika ask the AI how to spell?
How did Gopika feel when Amma asked to see the app?
qa.a: Watched and embarrassed, as if a spy had caught Gopika; the ears went hot.

qa.q: What rules did Gopika and Amma agree on?
qa.a: No AI after nine, never the full name or school, and friend worries can go to Amma too.

qa.q: Why does Amma worry about the AI app?
qa.a: It is new and she does not understand it yet, and she saw Gopika on it late at night.

grounding: A child who feels watched when a worried parent asks to see AI chats shares them openly, explains the use and agrees on rules.
